C.oracle: brute self-avoiding cycle search with type counts; executable construction validator

D.oracle: Dijkstra over actual legal adjacent-swap and prefix-delete state graph

E.oracle: full enumeration of all recursive-tree parent arrays and direct weighted distances
E.range: N=2..7, 4 random weight vectors per N

proof_equivalent_gates.C: A closed cycle must contain an even number of red (checkerboard-flipping) steps. If R=0, diagonal steps also force B even. Explicit constructions realize every remaining case: an orthogonal detour plus a simple diagonal-lattice path when R>0, or a rectangle in the diagonal lattice when R=0.
proof_equivalent_gates.D: Any execution induces a stable final deletion order of original occurrences. Adjacent swaps equal its inversion distance from A, and delete operations equal the number of equal-value runs; conversely any stable target order is realizable with exactly those costs.
proof_equivalent_gates.E: For random recursive trees, P(k ancestor of x)=1/k for k<x; for k<u<v, P(k ancestor of both)=2/(k(k+1)), so edge k separates u,v with probability 2(k-1)/(k(k+1)). Edge u separates with (u-1)/u, u<k<v with 1/k, and edge v with 1. Prefix sums give each query.

x1_reason: No frozen claim-grade M0 correctness failure. D requires a qualitatively new asymptotic architecture, so X1 is prohibited by protocol.
